business_scope.primary_industry_name: Fitness Biometric Tracking and Wellness Telemetry Apps

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (codified Napoleon-based codes; dual judicial-order system with repartition between judiciaire and administratif)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: France-US Double Taxation Prevention Treaty (1994, as amended by protocols)
France-China Agreement for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion (1984, effective 1986)
EU-Canada Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA - FTA)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Code monétaire et financier (CMF), Articles L561-1 et seq. (AML/CFT); Code de commerce, Articles L561-46 et seq. and R561-1 to R561-27 (UBO register filings); Décret n° 2020-115 of 14 February 2020 (ownership thresholds); French Customs Code (sanctions screening); Tracfin guidelines.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation / Existence of ultimate shareholder entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registrar in the shareholder's country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney in favor of the local incorporation agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Shareholder's home country notary public or public authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (if not a Hague Apostille state)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport copy of the proposed SARL manager (gérant) and UBOs

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, gérant, signatories, and UBOs against Tracfin terrorist-financing lists, EU Council consolidated sanctions, UN Security Council consolidated list, and OFAC SDN list as risk-mitigation policy. Enhanced due diligence required under CMF Article L561-6 for any observed PEP status under CMF Articles L561-2-1 to L561-10-1.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises and the Registre National du Commerce et des Sociétés (RNCS) operated through the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce / Infogreffe
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate name must be compatible with French public policy and gearing; initial mandatory use of Latin script. Foreign-language names are permissible only when transliterated/re-engineered into French or Latin characters. Any acronym, abbreviation, or legal-form indication must not mislead the public regarding the entity nature. For digital apps, the trade name can run in English, but the legal dénomination sociale must satisfy the French registrar.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon RNCS or Greffe refusal, the applicant must first submit an administrative re-examination request to the same Greffe within 30 days. If the refusal is maintained, a formal appeal may be filed before the Tribunal judiciaire (competent civil chamber) represented by counsel within 15 days of notification; alternatively, the applicant can amend the proposed name and create a new reservation.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Acceptable for digital health app activity: a commercial domiciliation agreement with an authorized third-party domiciliation company is lawful under Law n° 2014-626. The registered office must remain in metropolitan France or overseas département, with effective receipt of postal and legal documents. No physical personnel presence on-site is required for incorporation substance, but the company must have at least a French registered address and a legally valid commercial lease or domiciliation contract.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 15% standard likelihood of unannounced on-site inspection; if the company claims Research Tax Credit (CIR) or holds significant tax registrations, or if the office is a virtual domiciliation provider, inspection likelihood rises to 40%.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for compliance assistance

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L.210-1 to L.210-6, L.223-1 to L.223-43; implementing decree for SARL formalities and registration with the Registre du commerce et des sociétés.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Guichet unique operated by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI), transmitted to the Greffe du tribunal de commerce for registration in the Registre du commerce et des sociétés (RCS).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Formulaire M0 (electronic declaration of incorporation filed through the Guichet unique, supplemented by uploaded statutory documents).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum share capital for an SARL. Share capital is freely fixed in the articles. Cash contributions must be fully paid up and deposited into a segregated escrow account with a French bank, or held by a notaire, until the company is registered; the depositary releases the funds only upon presentation of the Kbis.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The shareholders hereby adopt the following first board resolutions. 1. Subscription. The share capital set forth in the articles of association is fully subscribed and allotted to the shareholders against their cash and in-kind contributions. 2. Registered office. The registered office is adopted at the address indicated in the company's articles of association for legal and administrative purposes. 3. Officers. [Name] is appointed as sole gérant for the term stated in the articles, with authority to manage the company, open and operate bank accounts, execute contracts, and represent the company. 4. Implementation. The gérant is expressly authorised to sign, file, and publish all incorporation documents and to discharge statutory registration deadlines.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the articles of association and appointment of the first manager
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: All founding shareholders and the first gérant; a notaire is required only if real property is contributed or if a notarized deed is elected.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare and sign the statuts specifying legal form, corporate purpose, share capital, allocation of quotas, registered office, duration, management powers, and appointment of the first gérant. The gérant must sign an acceptance and a declaration of eligibility. For cash contributions, state that the funds are blocked in escrow; for in-kind contributions, annex a contribution report if required.
required_dossiers: Draft and signed articles of association
Official identification documents of each shareholder and the gérant
Acceptance of appointment signed by the first gérant
Proof of registered office address
Declaration of absence of criminal conviction for the gérant
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry notes a defect in the statuts, the shareholders may adopt a rectifying unanimous resolution and submit amended articles through the Guichet unique without re-commencing the process.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Blocking of cash contributions in an escrow account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French commercial bank, notaire, or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations as depositary.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary account in the name of the company-in-formation and deposit the full amount of cash subscriptions. Obtain a certificate of funds deposit (attestation du dépositaire des fonds). The depositary will release funds to the gérant only after registration, upon presentation of the Kbis extract.
required_dossiers: Certificate of capital deposit issued by the bank or notaire
Schedule of cash subscriptions
Extract of the capital clause from the draft articles
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses to open the escrow account, the promoter may apply to the Banque de France for designation of a depositary bank through the legal assignment mechanism for business accounts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of the incorporation dossier to the Guichet unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet unique legal formalities portal of the INPI, with transmission to the Greffe du tribunal de commerce of the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the M0 electronic declaration and upload the certified true copy of the signed articles, certificate of capital deposit, proof of registered office occupancy, identity documents, and manager declarations. Submit the dossier online and retain the electronic acknowledgement of receipt showing the date of filing.
required_dossiers: Completed and electronically signed M0 form
Signed articles of association
Certificate of capital deposit
Proof of registered office address (lease, utility bill, or domiciliation agreement)
Identity document and eligibility declaration of the gérant
Identity documents of all shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Guichet unique returns a complement request, the filer receives an electronic list of missing or invalid documents and has a statutory cure period to upload the required items. Failure to cure leads to rejection, but the corrected dossier may be resubmitted without additional fees.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration by the Greffe and issuance of the Kbis extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du tribunal de commerce holding the Registre du commerce et des sociétés.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Greffe verifies the legality of the dossier, records the SARL in the RCS, assigns the SIREN number, and issues the official Kbis extract proving legal existence. The creation is automatically published to the BODACC legal gazette.
required_dossiers: Electronic dossier transmitted by the Guichet unique
Signed and certified articles of association
Certificate of capital deposit
Proof of registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If registration is refused, the Greffe must state the reasons. The filer may correct the identified defects and resubmit through the Guichet unique, or contest the refusal before the supervising judge of the commercial court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INSEE, URSSAF, local tax office (Service des Impôts des Entreprises), and commercial registry notifications.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receipt of the Kbis, open the definitive corporate bank account, obtain the SIRET and VAT identifiers, register with URSSAF for employer and social declarations, and complete tax account setup. Ensure corporate books (shareholders' minute book and share registry) are opened and, where applicable, file compliance declarations for the digital health app activity.
required_dossiers: Kbis extract
SIREN registration notice
Bank account confirmation
Tax and social registration forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If activation of the tax or social identifiers is delayed, the company may use the Kbis and SIREN notice to demand rectification from INSEE, and any overdue social declarations may be filed under the tutelary régularisation procedure with URSSAF.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable - no industrial establishment for ISIC 6201 software activity. Workplace inspection jurisdiction is exercised by DREETS for occupational health and safety in service-sector premises.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No operating license or manufacturing permit required for a non-medical fitness app tracker; only ordinary business and office occupancy requirements apply.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Direction régionale de l'environnement, de l'aménagement et du logement (DREAL) in coordination with the local prefecture.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - no registration or full EIA applicable because the activity is a purely digital service not listed under the French nomenclature of classified installations for environmental protection.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater, VOC, or air-emission threshold applies. Office waste, electronic equipment, and batteries must be removed by registered waste operators in compliance with the French Code de l'environnement.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: For a standard office or coworking suite, no prior civil-defense permit or structural-load inspection is required. The occupier must maintain fire evacuation routes, smoke detection, fire extinguishers, accessible first-aid equipment, and an up-to-date DUERP occupational risk assessment. If the building is open to the public, the relevant ERP authorization under the Fire Code must be verified with the local mairie.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction générale des finances publiques (DGFiP), through the relevant Service des impôts des entreprises (SIE) and the official impots.gouv.fr portal. Business creation data are generally transmitted through the Institut national de la propriété industrielle (INPI) Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A French SARL obtains its SIREN and SIRET identifiers through registration with the Registre national des entreprises via the INPI Guichet unique. The DGFiP then assigns or confirms the French tax identification details, including the intracommunity VAT number (FR followed by a two-digit control key and the nine-digit SIREN), after review of the registration file. A foreign entity without a French establishment requests tax registration from the competent non-resident tax service or relevant SIE, submitting constitutional documents, proof of business activity, identification of directors and beneficial owners, French representative details where required, and evidence of the French VAT nexus. VAT registration is separate from corporate income tax registration and may be required before taxable transactions commence.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A SARL is generally subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés, IS). An election for income-tax treatment (impôt sur le revenu, IR) may be available under statutory conditions, including for certain family SARLs and qualifying small companies for a limited period. The election is not a general United States-style check-the-box regime. France does not provide a general elective hybrid-mismatch classification mechanism for SARLs; anti-hybrid rules implement the EU Anti-Tax Avoidance Directive.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: French value added tax (taxe sur la valeur ajoutée, VAT), coordinated with the European Union VAT system.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For the domestic French VAT franchise regime, the principal annual turnover threshold is EUR 37,500 for services, including most electronically supplied or digitally delivered services when France is the place of taxation. The enhanced threshold is EUR 41,250. The goods threshold is EUR 85,000, with an enhanced threshold of EUR 93,500. These are exemption thresholds, not a universal VAT nexus rule. Cross-border digital services can require registration notwithstanding domestic franchise thresholds. For EU business-to-consumer electronically supplied services, the EUR 10,000 EU-wide threshold and the One Stop Shop regime may apply.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France does not currently operate a universal real-time VAT clearance system. The mandated model uses approved private Partner Dematerialization Platforms (PDPs), with the public invoicing portal serving as the central data-routing and reporting infrastructure. All French businesses must be capable of receiving electronic invoices from 1 September 2026. Issuance of domestic B2B electronic invoices is scheduled from 1 September 2026 for large and medium-sized enterprises and from 1 September 2027 for small and micro-enterprises. Electronic reporting applies to relevant cross-border B2B and B2C transactions and certain domestic payment data. Invoices must contain mandatory French and EU VAT information, use an approved structured or hybrid format, and be transmitted through the prescribed platform infrastructure.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported from France to a destination outside the European Union may be supplied without French VAT if the supplier can prove export and exit from the EU customs territory, normally through electronic customs exit certification or equivalent legally accepted evidence. Intra-EU supplies of goods are generally VAT-exempt with a right of deduction when the customer has a valid VAT number and the transport and reporting conditions are satisfied; this is technically an exemption rather than domestic zero-rating. Services supplied to a business customer established outside France are generally taxed at the customer's place of establishment under the B2B place-of-supply rule and are invoiced without French VAT, subject to customer-status and evidence requirements. Digitally supplied B2C services are generally taxed where the consumer resides, potentially through OSS or a non-Union registration. VAT input refunds require valid invoices, a direct business purpose, proper accounting, and evidence that the related transactions qualify for deduction.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Export customs declaration accepted through the French/EU customs system
Electronic proof of exit from the European Union customs territory, such as an exit result or equivalent customs certification
Commercial invoice identifying the supplier, customer, goods, values, VAT treatment, and applicable customs information
Transport evidence, such as bill of lading, airway bill, CMR consignment note, or carrier delivery record
Packing list and relevant export licence or regulatory certificate where applicable
For intra-EU supplies: customer VAT identification number, transport evidence, and required recapitulative statement documentation
For offshore services: customer business-status evidence, contractual documentation, service delivery records, and evidence supporting the customer's establishment outside France
Accounting records and VAT return schedules supporting the zero-rated or outside-scope treatment
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: France has no general statutory foreign-exchange repatriation deadline applicable to export VAT relief. The taxpayer must nevertheless retain reliable proof of export, customer status, transport, contractual performance, and accounting treatment for the applicable record-retention period. Unsupported or fraudulent export treatment may result in reassessment of VAT, recovery of wrongly deducted input VAT, late-payment interest generally calculated at 0.20% per month, and tax penalties commonly ranging from 10% for non-compliance to 40% for deliberate conduct and 80% for fraudulent manoeuvres or abuse of rights, subject to statutory conditions. Customs violations may trigger separate duties, fines, seizure, or other customs sanctions. Serious intentional tax fraud may also lead to criminal prosecution, including imprisonment and substantial fines under the French Tax Code.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (central bank and balance-of-payments authority), acting with the Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution (ACPR) for bank licensing and the Direction Générale du Trésor for exchange-control and foreign-investment matters.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France applies full capital-account and current-account convertibility under Article 63 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union. No prior FX licence or exchange-control approval is required for subscription of SARL capital, profit remittance, dividend distribution, royalty payment, or liquidation proceeds transfer by non-resident shareholders. Practical restrictions are not FX controls but bank compliance, TRACFIN suspicious-transaction reporting, and mandatory withholding-tax documentation where the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive or a bilateral tax treaty is invoked. Funds may be maintained in EUR or any freely convertible currency, and no special non-resident account category is imposed.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender, forced conversion, or fixed repatriation deadline exists for French export proceeds. A French SARL may collect export receivables in the currency of the invoice and retain them in a normal foreign-currency bank account. The only obligations are statistical reporting of cross-border transactions to the Banque de France for balance-of-payments purposes when above de minimis thresholds and, where an export of digital-health services is zero-rated for VAT, maintenance of commercial evidence of the recipient's EU or non-EU status.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital escrow (blocage de fonds) and operational EUR/USD current account
Capital escrow and operational EUR/USD account with integrated treasury/FX desk

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole S.A. (LCL, Le Crédit Lyonnais S.A.)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational current account and capital deposit attestation for SARL formation

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: CIC (Crédit Industriel et Commercial), Crédit Mutuel Alliance Fédérale
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational account and escrow/blocked funds certificate for capital injection

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium-High for operational EUR and SEPA flows when the EMI holds a valid EU electronic-money institution or credit-institution passport under PSD2/EMD2 and is registered with ACPR. High for low-cost remote onboarding, but an EMI cannot lawfully grant credit, offer overdrafts, or provide the same depositor protection as a bank; therefore it is not recommended as the sole escrow bank for SARL registered capital. Non-EU or non-passported offshore EMIs are non-viable and should not receive corporate treasury funds.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote opening is permitted for a standard-risk French SARL. Under French AML/KYC rules (Code monétaire et financier, Art. R561-5-2), bank identity verification of managers and beneficial owners may be completed by delegated third-party or video identity verification (PVID); no statutory rule compels physical board presence. In practice, the bank may require a video interview with at least one managing director (gérant), and may impose physical verification only for non-EEA passport holders, complex trust/offshore chains, or failed electronic UBO verification. Recommended posture: prepare a remote-compliant KYC pack with certified IDs and have the French-resident gérant available for interview.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume, low-ticket digital micro-payments from Apple IAP and Google Play Billing, creating an unusually high number of credit entries relative to declared turnover and payroll.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apple/Google settlement statements; in-app purchase tax-footprint reconciliation; monthly subscriber/DAU analytics; audited or accountant-reviewed financial statements; CNIL/DPIA privacy documentation; app store legal terms; and an accountant's source-of-funds memorandum.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-EU beneficial owners or a multinational group holding more than 25% of the SARL, especially where inbound capital originates from a low-tax jurisdiction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Filing proof of the Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (RBE); notarised UBO declarations; certified passports; corporate chart and constitutional documents; sanctions/PEP screening output; tax residence certificates; and a legal opinion from a French avocat if the chain includes a trust or fiduciary.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Intermediate payment aggregators, crypto-currency exposure, or unexplained pass-through wallets between the app stores and the SARL bank account.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed PSP/aggregator agreements; settlement detail per transaction; bank traceability map; a written no-digital-asset acceptance or, where applicable, ACPR DASP registration evidence; and audit-ready flow diagrams of the full cash path.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Preferred rail: SEPA Credit Transfer in EUR, or SWIFT MT103 for non-EUR, with remittance field coded 'Apport en capital' or 'Compte courant d'associé' and aligned to the Banque de France balance-of-payments nomenclature for direct investment capital flows. For SARL formation, the bank must first hold and block the subscribed capital and issue a certificate of funds deposit (attestation de blocage de fonds / certificat du dépositaire), which the gérant files with the Registre du commerce. Once registration is complete, the blocked funds are released to the SARL operational account. Supporting verification: signed share-subscription resolution, payment receipt, copy of the constitutive act, and UBO declarations screened by the bank.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For digital-health service trade settlements, use SEPA Instant or SEPA Credit Transfer for EUR suppliers and SWIFT MT103 (gpi) for non-EUR invoices, always inserting the underlying contract/invoice reference in field 70. When importing physical wellness hardware or devices, use a documentary commercial letter of credit governed by UCP600 with SWIFT MT700 issuance and MT103 cover payment; for smaller disbursements, use an automated MT103 payable upon presentation of invoice and customs evidence. All international payments should be routed through TARGET2/SEPA for euro legs and SWIFT gpi for correspondent clearing to non-EU banks, with full sanctions screening at every hop.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright forward FX (plain vanilla EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, EUR/CNH) for firm or highly expected commercial receipts/payments up to 12 months tenor
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for soft-currency exposures when physical delivery is legally or operationally unavailable
FX swaps (swap de change) for short-term treasury liquidity and cross-currency working capital rotation
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) for long-term shareholder loans or committed capex inflows
OTC European-style currency options and zero-cost collars used solely to hedge app-store and cloud-supplier currency exposure, executed under ISDA with an ACPR-licensed counterparty

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced rate of 15.00% for small and medium-sized enterprises on taxable profits up to EUR 42,500 per fiscal year, provided the statutory corporate income tax rate was at least 25.00% and turnover does not exceed EUR 10,000,000. Standard corporate income tax rate is 25.00%. No general tax holiday applies, but the Crédit d'Impôt Recherche (research tax credit) and accelerated depreciation for software and digital assets may reduce effective taxation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form No. 2065 (Déclaration de résultat) together with annexes 2051 to 2059-G, filed electronically via the official French portal impots.gouv.fr (GTC/EDI system).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a fiscal year ending 31 December, the return must be filed by the second working day after 1 May (generally 3 May). For other fiscal year-ends, the return is due within 30 days after the end of the fiscal year. The balance of corporate income tax is payable at the same deadline.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net sales and turnover, including gross app store revenue before platform commissions, from the digital health fitness application.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The French SARL files as resident; non-resident shareholders do not file this return. For a non-resident enterprise without a French permanent establishment, Form 2065 is not applicable; attributing French-source digital revenue requires a permanent establishment assessment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating expenses: software development, cloud hosting, marketing, employee salaries, and platform fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Related-party expenses paid to non-resident affiliates must be arm's length and supported by transfer pricing documentation.
Depreciation is deductible on assets owned by the French entity; shareholder-financed assets require arm's length interest and compliance with thin capitalization rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable profit before corporate income tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border transfers or cost contributions must be documented at arm's length to prevent profit shifting.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Special deductions and tax credits, including Crédit d'Impôt Recherche and the reduced SME rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Credits must relate to French eligible activities; artificial attribution of foreign R&D to the French entity risks recharacterization.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a 10% increase of the tax due, escalating to 40% for intentional late filing and 80% for tax evasion. Monthly interest of 0.20% accrues, plus a 5% late-payment penalty. Directors may be jointly liable if the failure is intentional.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief, the non-resident beneficial owner must (1) submit a Tax Residency Certificate issued by the competent foreign tax authority, (2) complete and file Form 5000 with the French tax administration (DGFiP), and (3) demonstrate beneficial ownership and absence of abuse. EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive may eliminate withholding tax for qualifying EU parent entities, subject to Form 5000 and holding period requirements.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic statutory rates: 30.00% for royalties and interest, subject to treaty reduction. Under EU Interest & Royalties Directive, payments between associated companies may be exempt from withholding tax. Treaty rates typically range 0%–15% for interest and 0%–10% for royalties depending on the applicable DTA.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not apply a separate Economic Substance Regulation regime comparable to the UAE. However, the abuse of law doctrine (abus de droit),, the 'weak link' doctrine (maillon faible), EU ATAD anti-hybrid rules, interest limitation rules, and CFC rules collectively require the French SARL to demonstrate real substance: employees, premises, decision-making, and risk-bearing capacity. Artificial arrangements lacking substance are recharacterized.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate under-declaration of app subscription revenue, hidden foreign bank accounts, false invoices, or fictitious expenses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative 80% increase of tax evaded plus 0.20% monthly interest. Criminal penalties: fine up to EUR 1,500,000 for legal entities or 50% of evaded tax, and imprisonment up to 7 years for individuals.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be jointly and severally liable, subject to asset freezes, travel bans, civil restitution, and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: French SARL or cross-border structure without real economic activity, staffing, premises, or risk-taking, used solely to channel digital revenue to low-tax jurisdictions or claim treaty benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Disallowance of tax benefits, 80% penalty for abuse of law, application of CFC rules, and reassessment of profits. Potential permanent establishment exposure in other jurisdictions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face personal liability for tax reassessments, civil restitution, management bans, and potential criminal sanctions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving payments through opaque unlicensed channels, failure to identify ultimate beneficial owners (UBO), failure to file UBO declarations with the RCS, or unexplained third-party transfers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine up to EUR 75,000 for natural persons and EUR 375,000 for legal entities; seizure of funds under the French Monetary and Financial Code.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Criminal sanctions, disqualification from management, and civil seizure of personal assets for complicity in money laundering or aggravated tax fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to prepare or produce Local File / Master File for cross-border related-party transactions, or non-arm's length intra-group invoicing.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine of EUR 10,000 per undocumented tax year; reassessment at arm's length; 5% increase of reassessed amount; additional 80% penalty in cases of bad faith.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Where the corporate veil is pierced, directors may be held personally liable for tax adjustments and interest.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Unjustified treaty or EU Directive relief on distributions, failure to hold proper TRC, or mischaracterizing equity distributions as loans.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Withholding tax plus 80% penalty and 0.20% monthly interest; restitution of tax credits; exclusion from reduced rates for up to 5 years; publication of sanction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Knowing preparation of false treaty relief claims may result in criminal fraud liability, imprisonment, and commercial management prohibitions.
